product.name: Entity Runtime
product.lede: Declare an entity's fields, lifecycle, operations, rules and events as data. A deterministic Rust kernel answers each requested operation with the complete next decision, or a typed refusal that changes nothing. It reads no clock, file or network: storage, identity, time and side effects stay with the application around it.
product.meta: Rust libraries and the entity command · Linux, macOS, Windows · Apache-2.0

sections.title: One boundary between a proposal and durable state.
sections.lede: The agent chooses a named operation. The trusted shell supplies authority and canonical state. The kernel decides, from data.

items.title: Policy outside the prompt
items.description: Schema, lifecycle, operations, rules and events are a validated definition with closed keys, not prose a model reinterprets on every call.

items.title: Operations, not patches
items.description: Callers ask for approve or reject, never for a writable status field. Every move is a declared transition with its own arguments and rules.

items.title: Refusals are data
items.description: A refusal names its kind and the rule, state or path that caused it. Missing evidence is unknown, not false.

items.title: Decisions carry their record
items.description: Command, definition, changes and events are kept with caller-supplied provenance; replay re-runs the decision instead of trusting it.

items.title: No silent overwrites
items.description: Every commit names the revision it was decided on. A stale writer is refused; an exact retry gets the original result back.

items.title: One model, many surfaces
items.description: Lifecycle graphs, entity pages with OpenAPI and AsyncAPI, MCP tools and a generated Rust command come from the same definitions.

steps.title: The agent proposes
steps.description: A named operation and the domain arguments it was delegated.

steps.title: The shell supplies trust
steps.description: Canonical state, identity, authority, record id, time and the expected revision.

steps.title: The kernel decides
steps.description: Transition, schema, preconditions, assignments, invariants and events, in a fixed order.

steps.title: The provider commits
steps.description: State, history and events in one write, or a typed refusal that changes nothing.

sections.title: Released, and held by named tests.
sections.lede: Shipped means released in a tagged version and held by a test or gate step in the repository. Planned means a draft on the plan.

tools.name: AEP
tools.description: Governed planning. The lifecycle of each kind of planning artifact is an Entity Runtime definition, and entity-core decides every move.

tools.name: Eventlog
tools.description: Append-only event storage. entity-eventlog keeps complete recorded state on its file, SQLite, PostgreSQL and tree providers.
